result.markdown: --- title: "[RandomSurvivalForest]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} A random survival forest: a bagged ensemble of log-rank survival trees. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_forest.py#L915-L970){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python RandomSurvivalForest( *, n_estimators=100, max_depth=None, min_samples_split=6, min_samples_leaf=3, max_features="sqrt", bootstrap=True, oob_score=False, engine="numpy", random_state=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each tree is grown on a bootstrap sample of the data and considers a random subset of covariates at every split, following Ishwaran et al. (2008). At each node the split threshold is chosen to maximize the log-rank separation between the child groups. Predictions average the per-tree cumulative-hazard functions across the ensemble; the scalar risk score is the summed ensemble cumulative hazard (mortality). Averaging many decorrelated trees yields a low-variance, well-calibrated non-parametric survival model that captures non-linearities and interactions without a proportional-hazards assumption. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n_estimators]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of trees in the forest. [max_depth]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum depth of each tree (`None` for unlimited). [min_samples_split]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[6]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Minimum node size eligible for splitting. [min_samples_leaf]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[3]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Minimum subjects in each child of a split. [max_features]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["sqrt"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Covariates considered per split: `"sqrt"` (default), `"log2"`, an int, a float, or `None`. [bootstrap]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to grow each tree on a bootstrap sample (required for `oob_score` and `variable_importance`). [oob_score]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to compute an out-of-bag concordance estimate after fitting. [engine]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["numpy"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Compute backend for the split search: `"numpy"` (default, deterministic) or `"numba"` (faster on large datasets, requires the `fast` extra; produces a statistically equivalent fit that may differ in tie-breaking). `"auto"` uses Numba when available. [random_state]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Seed or `numpy.random.Generator` for bootstrap sampling and per-node feature selection. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a forest on the bundled `lung` dataset and inspect the out-of-bag concordance: ::: {#70776e5a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and build a right-censored response lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="pandas").dropna(subset=["ph.ecog", "ph.karno"]) y = gw.Surv.right(lung["time"], event=(lung["status"] == 2)) cols = ["age", "sex", "ph.ecog", "ph.karno", "wt.loss"] # Fit the forest with an out-of-bag score rsf = gw.RandomSurvivalForest( n_estimators=100, oob_score=True, random_state=0 ).fit(y, lung[cols]) rsf ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` RandomSurvivalForest (100 log-rank trees, max_features='sqrt') n = 213, events = 151, features = 5 out-of-bag concordance = 0.6009 ``` ::: :::
